column1: # LOG-DEAD-SITES.tsv - reference `log.*` calls the reference CONTAINS but NEVER REACHES.
# These are subtracted from the site inventory before every coverage figure, and from the
# `expected` count of the file they live in. They are NOT exclusions: an exclusion retires a
# whole reference FILE, and `font/shaper/coretext.zig` still has four genuinely live sites
# alongside its four dead ones. Using the file-level mechanism here would erase real debt and
# spend the exclusion budget on something that is not an exclusion.
# oracle_file  reference path at pin 20abdb50a.
# line         the exact line of the `log.*` call. A line that is not a live reference log
#              site at the pin is RED - a declaration that corresponds to nothing removes
#              nothing and hides a drift.
# kind         one of: unreachable-private, commented-caller, dead-branch, unreferenced-pub.
#              `unreferenced-pub` (task S-1c) is a site in a `pub fn` that nothing in the
#              reference tree names (Zig analyses lazily, so it is never compiled). It is
#              VERIFIED: the gate's tree index must show the enclosing `pub fn`'s name
#              written nowhere but its definition and never quoted, or the row is RED.
# reason       mandatory. A declaration with no reason is RED.
# THE CHECK THAT MAKES THIS NET-NEW COVERAGE RATHER THAN A SUBTRACTION (R5): a port emission
# carrying a declared-dead site's MESSAGE is RED. Nothing else in this gate can catch someone
# faithfully restoring a call the reference never makes - every count check would applaud it -
# and "read the preserved comment and add the call beneath it" is the standard method that
# produces exactly that. This plan has already found three genuine instances of the port
# emitting what the reference does not.
# An UNDECLARED dead site is undetectable by construction: nothing in the text says a function
# is never called. The cap below is therefore the only thing stopping this becoming an escape
# hatch the way the exclusion list nearly did. Two-way ratchet; a missing directive BLOCKS.
#!dead-site-cap entries=15

column4: task tail-s1b: `errdefer killCommand(&cmd) catch |err| log.warn(...)` is registered at :1073, and every statement between it and the function's success `return` (:1076 `log.info`, :1078 the `self.process` assignment, :1079 the `return switch`) is infallible, so no error can leave the scope after it and the errdefer never runs. exec.rs keeps it as a comment (:3439-3446).

column4: task tail-s1b: `std.fmt.bufPrint(&comm_path_buf, "/proc/{d}/comm", .{ppid})` writes at most 6 + 10 + 5 = 21 bytes (a pid_t is at most 10 digits) into a `std.fs.max_path_bytes` buffer, so NoSpaceLeft cannot occur. The port's `format!` has no arm either.
